deductive-logic: St. George Stock's compact textbook introduces the classic art of deductive reasoning — syllogisms, propositions, and the rules of valid argument. Clear definitions and worked examples guide students through logic's traditional forms. Though newer methods have joined it, the book remains a lucid introduction to thinking straight.
by-pike-and-dyke-a-tale-of-the-rise-of-t: Henty returns to the Netherlands' struggle for freedom, following a young Englishman through the sieges and sea-fights of the Dutch revolt. Pike and dyke — war on land and water — fill this stirring tale of the rise of the Dutch Republic. History as adventure, Henty-style.
the-boy-aviators-polar-dash-or-facing-de: John Henry Goldfrap's boy aviators fly to the Antarctic in a polar dash full of ice, danger, and daring. Written in the heroic age of exploration, it thrilled young readers with the ultimate adventure. Early aviation meets the last continent.
tales-of-the-enchanted-islands-of-the-at: Thomas Wentworth Higginson gathers the legends of the enchanted Atlantic isles — Atlantis, Avalon, St. Brendan's isle, and more. Sailors' dreams and poets' fancies mingle in these charming tales. A delightful voyage through the mythology of the sea. Lost Atlantis, phantom saints, and isles of the blest drift through these dreamlike tales.
a-trip-to-scarborough-and-the-critic: Sheridan pairs his comedy A Trip to Scarborough with his immortal farce The Critic — the tale of Mr. Puff and his disastrous play. Two delights from the wittiest playwright of the age. Laughter, guaranteed. Town fops, Irish bluster, and Mr. Puff's theatrical disasters provide an evening of pure fun.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acrostic: This 1913 reference piece on the acrostic — the alphabetical psalms and Lamentations, verse by letter. Anthony Maas traces the Hebrew device. Sorrow spelled out from aleph to tau. Poetry's oldest form of order.
